The time taken for the current situation to end, especially the current war.

ex.ja: オリンピック選手は、大会期間中は選手村で生活します。

en: The cardinal number occurring after fourteen (14) and before sixteen (16).
An Irish traybake made with crushed digestive biscuits, marshmallows and glacé cherries combined with condensed milk and desiccated coconut.

ex.en: The committee is made up of fifteen members.
ex.ja: 委員会は１５人のメンバーから成る。

ex.en: There were fifteen persons injured in the accident.
ex.ja: その事故で１５人がけがをした。

ex.en: Get up fifteen minutes earlier in the morning.
ex.ja: 朝は１５分早く起きなさい。

note.ja: five + -teen（10）。「5と10」。

en: A mother of someone's parent.
A female ancestor or progenitor.

grandmother.ety: From Middle English graundmodre, grauntmoder, granmoder; equivalent to grand- + mother. Compare French grand-mère. Superseded earlier eldmother, eldermother.

ex.en: My grandmother gave me more than I wanted.
ex.ja: 私の祖母は私が欲しがる以上のものをくれた。

ex.en: The girl was called Elizabeth after her grandmother.
ex.ja: 女の子はおばあさんの名を取ってエリザベスと名付けられた。

ex.en: Grandmother makes a practice of keeping early hours.
ex.ja: 祖母には早寝早起きの習慣がある。

note.ja: grand（一世代上の）+ mother。「祖母」。

en: Unpleasantly rough to the touch or other senses.
Severe or cruel.

harsh.ety: From Middle English harsk, harisk(e), hask(e), herris. Century derived the term from Old Norse harskr (whence Danish harsk (“rancid”), dialectal Norwegian hersk, Swedish härsk, Swedish härsken); the Middle English Dictionary derives it from that and Middle Low German harsch (“rough”, literally “hairy”) (whence also German harsch), from haer (“hair”), from Old Saxon hār, from Proto-West Germanic *hār; the Oxford Dictionary of English derives it from Middle Low German alone.

ex.en: Traffic noise is very harsh to the ear.
ex.ja: 車の騒音はとても耳障りだ。

ex.en: I didn't mean to sound so harsh.
ex.ja: そんなに厳しく言ったつもりはなかったのです。

ex.en: I hope my last mail didn't sound too harsh.
ex.ja: 前のメールがきつく響かなかったことを願っています。

note.ja: 中英語 harsk（ざらざらした）から。北欧語に由来するとされる。「粗い」→「厳しい」。

en: A hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals, usually paired.
Any similar real or imaginary growth or projection such as the elongated tusk of a narwhal, the eyestalk of a snail, the pointed growth o…
Of an animal, to assault with the horns.
To furnish with horns.

ex.ja: あまり鼻にかけるな。

ex.en: The Van Horn family was rich.
ex.ja: ヴァンホーン家は裕福だった。

ex.en: Do you know what they call a French horn in French?
ex.ja: フレンチホルンってフランス語で何ていうか知ってる？

note.ja: 古英語 horn から。ラテン語 cornu（unicorn）と同じ祖先。「角」→ 角笛 →「ホルン・警笛」。

en: A rushed action.
An urgency.
To do things quickly.
Often with up, to speed up the rate of doing something.

hurry.ety:
From Middle English horien (“to rush, impel”), probably a variation of hurren (“to vibrate rapidly, buzz”), from Proto-Germanic *hurzaną (“to rush”) (compare Middle High German hurren (“to hasten”), Norwegian hurre (“to whirl around”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱers- (“to run”) (compare Latin currō (“to run”), Tocharian A kursär/Tocharian B kwarsär (“league; course”)). Related to hurr, horse, rush.
Alternative etymology derives hurry as a variant of harry.

ex.en: If you hurry, you'll catch up with him.
ex.ja: 急げば彼に追いつくでしょう。

ex.en: I think we'll make it if we hurry.
ex.ja: 急げば何とか間に合うと思います。

ex.en: Hurry up, or you will miss the train.
ex.ja: 急げ、さもないと列車に乗り遅れるよ。

note.ja: 16世紀からの語。擬音的な語とされる。「急ぐ」。

en: Exempt; not subject to.
Protected by inoculation, or due to innate resistance to pathogens.
A person who is not susceptible to infection by a particular disease

ex.ja: トムはその病気に絶対かからないと言った。

ex.en: She is always immune to criticism.
ex.ja: 彼女は常に批判に動じない。

ex.en: He is immune from taxes.
ex.ja: 彼は税金を免除されている。

en: An act, instance of, or state of expansion or increase in size, especially by injection of a gas or liquid.
An increase in the quantity of money, leading to a devaluation of existing money, adjusted for by way of higher nominal values.

ex.en: Last year's growth of income was 5% after inflation.
ex.ja: 昨年の所得の実質成長は５％だった。

ex.en: The government adopted strong measures to fight inflation.
ex.ja: 政府はインフレに対するために強硬な措置をとった。

ex.en: The newspaper called for the government to stop inflation.
ex.ja: その新聞は政府にインフレを止めるように求めた。

note.ja: inflate（膨らませる）+ -ion。in + flare（吹く）。「吹き込んで膨らませること」→ 通貨の「膨張」→「インフレ」。

en: One of the substances present in a mixture, especially food.
A necessary element to achieve a certain goal; a component.

ingredient.ety: From Middle French ingredient, from Latin ingrediens, present participle of ingredior (“to go or enter into or onto”).

ex.en: Add the rest of the ingredients.
ex.ja: 残りの材料を加えてください。

ex.en: This cake is made of the finest ingredients.
ex.ja: このケーキは最高の材料で作られている。

ex.en: I bought ingredients for curry on Sunday.
ex.ja: 日曜日、カレーの材料を買いました。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ gred（歩む・入る）+ ient。中に入り込むもの →「材料・成分・要素」。

en: The act of examining something, often closely.
An organization that checks that certain laws or rules are obeyed.

inspection.ety: From Middle French, from Old French inspeccion, from Latin īnspectiō (“examination, inspection”), from the verb īnspiciō (“to inspect”), from speciō (“to look at”). By surface analysis, inspect + -ion.

ex.en: The building did not pass a fire inspection.
ex.ja: その建物は火災の検査にとおらなかった。

ex.en: We conduct safety inspections here on a regular basis.
ex.ja: ここでは定期的に安全点検を実施します。

ex.en: I hope this makes it through baggage inspection.
ex.ja: 荷物検査で引っかからなければいいけど。

note.ja: in（中を）+ spect（見る）+ ion。中まで見ること →「検査・点検」。

en: The quality of being intense.
The degree of strength.

intensity.ety: From intense + -ity. Cf. also Medieval Latin intensitas.

ex.en: He was overwhelmed by the intensity of her love.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女の愛情の強さに圧倒された。

ex.en: We were shocked by the intensity of our mother's anger.
ex.ja: 母親の怒りの厳しさにびっくりした。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ tens（伸ばす）+ ity。ぴんと張りつめた度合い →「強さ・激しさ」。

en: The stock of an item on hand at a particular location or business.
A detailed list of all of the items on hand.
To take stock of the resources or items on hand; to produce an inventory.

inventory.ety: From Middle English inventorie, from Medieval Latin inventōrium, alteration of Late Latin inventārium, from Latin inveniō (“to find out”).

ex.en: We have adequate inventories of the product to meet local demand.
ex.ja: 地方の需要に応えるのに十分な製品の在庫がある。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ vent（来る）+ ory。（手元に）来たものの一覧 →「在庫（目録）・棚卸し」。

en: The act of inviting; solicitation; the requesting of a person's company.
A document or verbal message conveying an invitation.

invitation.ety: From Middle English invitacioun, ynvytacioun, from Latin invītātio, reinforced by Middle French invitation. By surface analysis, invite + -ation. Displaced native Middle English lathinge from Old English laþung (see dialectal English lathing).

ex.en: You have a standing invitation to join us.
ex.ja: いつおいでくださっても歓迎いたします。

ex.en: To my regret I cannot accept your invitation.
ex.ja: 残念なことに、あなたの招待に応じられない。

ex.en: I'm afraid that I can't accept your invitation.
ex.ja: あいにくご招待をお受けできないのですが。

note.ja: invite（招待する）+ -ation。「招待」。

Of or relating to the court system or the judicial branch of government.
That branch of government which is responsible for maintaining the courts of law and for the administration of justice.

en: To provide an acceptable explanation for.
To be a good reason behind a normally-unacceptable action; to warrant.

justify.ety: From Middle English justifien, from Old French justifier, from Late Latin justificare (“make just”), from Latin justus, iustus (“just”) + ficare (“make”), from facere, equivalent to just + -ify.

ex.en: The end does not always justify the means.
ex.ja: 目的さえよければどんな手段をとってもよいわけではない。

ex.en: The end does not necessarily justify the means.
ex.ja: 目的は必ずしも手段を正当化しない。

ex.en: Can you justify the use of violence?
ex.ja: 君は暴力行使を正当化することができますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 justificare ＝ justus（正しい）+ facere。「正しいとする」→「正当化する」。just と同じ。

en: To incline, deviate, or bend, from a vertical position; to be in a position thus inclining or deviating.
To incline in opinion or desire; to conform in conduct; often with to, toward, etc.
An inclination away from the vertical.
Slim; not fleshy.
Having little fat.

lean.ety:
From Middle English lenen (“to lean”), from Old English hleonian, hlinian (“to lean, recline, lie down, rest”), from Proto-West Germanic *hlinēn, from Proto-Germanic *hlināną (“to lean, incline”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱley-.
Cognate via Proto-Germanic with Middle Dutch leunen (“to lean”), German lehnen (“to lean”); via Proto-Indo-European with climate, cline.

ex.en: He leaned over to put on his shoes.
ex.ja: 彼は靴をはくためにかがんだ。

ex.en: The old man leaned on his staff.
ex.ja: その老人は杖にもたれた。

ex.en: The box is leaning to one side.
ex.ja: その箱は一方に傾いている。

note.ja: 「傾く」は古英語 hleonian から。「やせた」は古英語 hlǣne からで別語。

en: A spoken lesson or exposition, usually delivered to a group.
A class that primarily consists of a (weekly or other regularly held) lecture (as in sense 1), usually at college or university.
To teach (somebody) by giving a speech on a given topic.
To preach, to berate, to scold.

lecture.ety: From Middle English lecture, lectour, letture, letteur, lettur, lectury, from Medieval Latin or Late Latin lectura (“reading”), from Latin lectus, past participle of legō (“to read, recite”). Doublet of lector.

ex.en: The students sat still, listening to the lecture.
ex.ja: 学生達は身じろぎもせずに講義に聞き入っていた。

ex.en: A lot of people came to the lecture.
ex.ja: 講演には多数の出席者があった。

ex.en: When we arrived, the lecture had already begun.
ex.ja: 私たちが着くと講演はもう始まっていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 legere（読む）から。lect + ure。読み上げること →「講義・説教」。

en: In agreement with the principles of logic.
Reasonable.

logical.ety: From logic + -al. Displaced native Old English flitcræftlīċ.

ex.en: If something doesn't make sense, it probably isn't logical.
ex.ja: もしあることが意味を成さなければ、それは多分論理的でないのである。

ex.en: His view is quite logical.
ex.ja: 彼の意見はたいへん論理的である。

ex.en: That's reversing the logical order of things.
ex.ja: それでは本末転倒だ。

note.ja: logic（論理）+ -al。ギリシャ語 logikē（推論の技術）、logos（言葉・理性）。

en: Having meaning, significant.
Full of implication; heavy with unstated meaning.

ex.en: She gave me a meaningful look.
ex.ja: 彼女の態度は意味深長だった。

note.ja: meaning（意味）+ -ful。「意味のある」。

en: An instance of moving to live in another place for a while.
Seasonal moving of animals, as mammals, birds or fish, especially between breeding and non-breeding areas.

migration.ety: From Middle French migration and its source, Latin migrātiō, from the participle stem of migrō (“to migrate”). Morphologically migrate + -ion.

ex.en: This species holds the record for long-distance migration.
ex.ja: この種は長距離移動の記録を持っています。

note.ja: ラテン語 migrare（移る）から。migr + ation。移り住むこと →「移住・（鳥などの）渡り・（データの）移行」。

en: Any object used as a weapon by being thrown or fired through the air, such as stone, arrow or bullet.
A self-propelled projectile whose trajectory can be adjusted after it is launched.

missile.ety: From Latin missile (“thrown weapon, projectile”), neuter of missilis (“throwable, capable of being thrown”), from mittere (“to send”). From 1611. Compare Middle French missile (“projectile”), from 1636.

ex.en: The angry crowd threw missiles at the police.
ex.ja: 怒った群衆は警官隊に物を投げつけた。

ex.en: It will be a push-button war of nuclear missiles.
ex.ja: それは核ミサイルをボタン一つで操作し合う戦争になるだろう。

ex.en: The missile attack took a heavy toll of lives.
ex.ja: ミサイル攻撃で多くの人命が失われた。

note.ja: miss（送る・投げる）+ ile。投げ飛ばせるもの →「ミサイル・飛び道具」。

To animate; to propel; to cause to take action.

ex.ja: 教師達は生徒にやる気を起こさせるように努力している。

ex.en: I don't know what motivated me to come here.
ex.ja: どういうはずみでここに来たのか自分でもわからない。

ex.en: Tie up your hair! Get motivated! Right, let's begin!
ex.ja: 髪を束ねて、気合入れて、さぁ始めよう！

note.ja: mot（動く）+ iv + ate。人を動かす →「やる気にさせる・動機を与える」。

en: The intercardinal compass point halfway between west and north; specifically at a bearing of 315°.
Of, in or pertaining to the northwest; northwestern.
Situated toward or in the direction of the northwest; northwestward; northwesterly.
Towards or in the direction of the northwest; northwestwards.

northwest.ety: From Middle English northwest, from Old English norþwest, equivalent to north + west.

ex.en: Ecuador is a country situated in the northwest part of South America.
ex.ja: エクアドルは南米の北西部に位置する国である。

note.ja: north + west。「北西」。

en: The larger part of an organism, composed of tissues that perform similar functions.
A body of an organization dedicated to the performing of certain functions.

Doublet of organon, organum, and orgue.

ex.en: There is usually an organ in a church.
ex.ja: 教会には普通オルガンがあります。

ex.en: The stomach is one of the internal organs.
ex.ja: 胃は内臓の一つである。

ex.en: The brain is a very complex organ.
ex.ja: 脳は極めて複雑な臓器だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 organon（道具）から。「道具」→ 体の道具「器官」→ 楽器「オルガン」。organize と同じ。

en: A going of the rounds along the chain of sentinels and between the posts, by a guard, usually consisting of three or four men, to insure …
A movement, by a small body of troops beyond the line of outposts, to explore the country and gain intelligence of the enemy's whereabouts.
To go the rounds along a chain of sentinels; to traverse a police district or beat.
To go the rounds of, as a sentry, guard, or policeman

patrol.ety: From French patrouille, from Old French patrouille, patouille (“a night-watch”, literally “a tramping about”), from patrouiller, patouiller, patoiller (“to paddle or pudder in water, dabble with the feet, begrime, besmear”), from patte, pate (“paw, foot of an animal”), from Vulgar Latin *patta (“paw, foot”), from Frankish *patta (“paw, sole of the foot”), from Proto-Germanic *paþjaną, *paþōną (“to walk, tread, go, step, pace”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pent-, *(s)pat- (“path; to walk”), a variant of Proto-Indo-European *pent-, *pat- (“path; to go”); see find. Cognate with Dutch pa

ex.en: The patrol cars cover the whole of the area.
ex.ja: パトロールカーはその地区の全体を警備する。

ex.en: We saw a patrol car running at full speed.
ex.ja: 私たちはパトカーが全速力で走っているのを見た。

ex.en: He ran away at the sight of a police patrol.
ex.ja: 巡回中の警官を見て彼は逃げた。

note.ja: フランス語 patrouiller（泥の中を歩き回る）から。patte（足）。「歩き回る」→「巡回する」。

en: Nacre; mother-of-pearl.
A white color inspired by the shade of pearls.
To set or adorn with pearls, or with mother-of-pearl.
To cause to resemble pearls in shape; to make into small round grains.

pearl.ety: Inherited from Middle English perle, from Old French perle of uncertain etymology. To utter with a loud wailing voice or wordless cry.

keen.ety:
From Middle English kene (“bold, brave, sharp”), from Old English cēne (“keen, fierce, bold, brave, warlike, powerful; learned, clever, wise”), from Proto-Germanic *kōniz (“knowledgeable, skilful, experienced, clever, capable”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- (“to know”).
Cognate with Danish køn (“handsome, pretty”), Dutch kien (“smart, wise, able”), koen (“daring, valiant, doughty, courageous”), German kühn (“bold, daring, audacious, hardy, valiant, venturesome”), Icelandic kænn (“wise, crafty, clever, able”), Faroese kønur (“expert (in, on), experienced, skilful, able, capable”), Scots kee

ex.en: The kid has a keen sense of hearing.
ex.ja: その子の聴覚は鋭い。

ex.en: Competition is very keen in the car industry.
ex.ja: 自動車産業では競争が激しい。

ex.en: He seemed to be very keen on music.
ex.ja: 彼は音楽にとても興味がありそうだった。

note.ja: 古英語 cēne（大胆な）から。「鋭い」→「熱心な」。

en: Of two (or, rarely, more than two) things: smaller in size (littler), in value, in importance etc.
In plant and animal names, denotes a smaller kind.
One who is lesser; an inferior.

From less + -er.

ex.en: Both choices are bad, so choose the lesser evil.
ex.ja: どちらもよくない選択なので、まだましなほうを選びなさい。

note.ja: less の比較級を重ねた形。「より小さい・劣った」。

en: obligatory; required or commanded by authority.
Of, being or relating to a mandate.
A sign or line that require the path of the disc to be above, below or to one side of it.

mandatory.ety: From Late Latin mandatorius (“of or belonging to a mandator”), from mandātor (“one who commands”), equivalent to mandate + -ory; see mandate.

ex.en: Age discrimination is illegal and retirement is mandatory in only a few occupations.
ex.ja: 年齢による差別は法律違反であり、退職が強制されるのは、ほんの少数の職業においてである。

note.ja: mand（命じる）+ at + ory。命じられた →「義務的な・強制の」。

en: The branch of physics that deals with the action of forces on material objects with mass.
The design and construction of machines.

ex.en: Those mechanics are paid as much as ten thousand yen per hour.
ex.ja: あの修理工たちは時給一万円ももらっている。

note.ja: mechanic（機械の）+ -s（学問）。ギリシャ語 mēkhanē（機械）。「力学・仕組み」。mechanism と同じ。

en: Just, only; no more than, pure and simple, neither more nor better than might be expected.
Boundary, limit; a boundary-marker; boundary-line.
To decide upon the position of a boundary; to position it on a map.

mere.ety:
From Middle English mere, mer, from Anglo-Norman meer, from Old French mier, from Latin merus (“pure, unmixed, undiluted”), from Proto-Indo-European *mer- (“to sparkle, gleam”).
Cognate with Old English āmerian, āmyrian (“to purify, examine, revise”). The Middle English word was perhaps influenced by or conflated with sound-alike Middle English mere (“glorious, noble, splendid, fine, pure”), from Old English mǣre (“famous, great, excellent, sublime, splendid, pure, sterling”), from Proto-West Germanic *mārī, from Proto-Germanic *mērijaz.

ex.en: You are no longer a mere child.
ex.ja: 君はもはや子供なんかではない。

ex.en: You must give close attention to the merest details.
ex.ja: ほんの些細なことにも細心の注意を払わなければならない。

ex.en: The mere sight of a dog made her afraid.
ex.ja: 犬を見ただけで彼女は怖がった。

note.ja: ラテン語 merus（混じりけのない）から。「混じりけのない」→「ほんの・単なる」。merely と同じ。

en: An event that appears inexplicable by the laws of nature and so is held to be supernatural in origin.
A fortunate outcome that prevails despite overwhelming odds against it.
To affect by a miracle; to work a miracle upon.

miracle.ety: From Middle English miracle, from Old French miracle, from Latin mīrāculum (“object of wonder”), from mīror (“to wonder at”), from mīrus (“wonderful”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meyh₂- (“to smile, to be astonished”). Doublet of milagro and miraculum. Partially displaced native wonder, from Old English wundor (“miracle, wonder”).

ex.en: Our escape was nothing short of a miracle.
ex.ja: われわれの脱出は奇跡というほかなかった。

ex.en: The escape was nothing less than a miracle.
ex.ja: その脱出は全く奇跡に他ならなかった。

ex.en: Christ is believed to have worked many miracles.
ex.ja: キリストは多くの奇跡を行ったと信じられている。

note.ja: ラテン語 miraculum（驚くべきもの）から。mirari（驚く）。marvel、mirror と同じ mir。

en: A mixture of water and soil or fine grained sediment.
A plaster-like mixture used to texture or smooth drywall.
To make muddy or dirty; to apply mud to (something).
To make turbid.

mud.ety: From Middle English mud, mudde, mode, probably a borrowing from Middle Dutch mod, modde or Middle Low German mudde, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *mud-, *mudra- (“mud”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *mū-, *mew- (“moist”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Mudde (“mud”), Middle High German mot (“mud”), Swedish modd (“slush”). Compare also suffixed variants English mother (“vinegar-forming sediment in alcohol”), West Frisian modder (“mud”), Dutch modder (“mud”), German Low German Mudder (“mud”), German Moder (“moldiness, mildew, decay”), Danish mudder (“mud”). Alternative etymology suggests th

ex.en: Please remove the mud from your shoes.
ex.ja: 靴から泥を取り除いてください。

ex.en: The car got stuck in the mud.
ex.ja: 車がぬかるみにはまって動けなくなった。

ex.en: The boy returned with his face covered with mud.
ex.ja: 少年は顔中泥んこになって帰って来た。

note.ja: 中世低地ドイツ語 mudde から。「泥」。

en: The act of observing, and the fact of being observed (see observance)
The act of noting and recording some event; or the record of such noting.

observation.ety:
From Middle English observacion, borrowed from Middle French observacion. Also a borrowing from French observation and a learned borrowing from Latin observātiō(n-).
Morphologically observe + -ation.

ex.en: A careful observation will show you the difference.
ex.ja: 注意深く観察すれば違いがわかるでしょう。

ex.en: Science is based on very careful observations.
ex.ja: 科学は非常に綿密な観察に基づいている。

ex.en: Close observation is necessary for the experiment.
ex.ja: その実験には綿密な観察が必要だ。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ serv（見守る）+ ation。注意深く見守ること →「観察・意見」。

en: To be under an obligation to give something back to someone or to perform some action for someone.
To have debt; to be in debt.

From Middle English owen, from Old English āgan, from Proto-West Germanic *aigan (“to own”), from Proto-Germanic *aiganą, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eh₂óyḱe (“to possess, own”), reduplicated stative of *h₂eyḱ- (“to own”). See also own, ought.
Cognate with Sanskrit ईष्टे (īṣṭe, “to own, possess”).

ex.en: I owe what I am to my father.
ex.ja: 私がいるのは父のおかげです。

ex.en: I owe what I am today to education.
ex.ja: 私が今日あるのは、教育のおかげです。

ex.en: I owe what I am to my mother.
ex.ja: 私が今日あるのは母親のおかげだ。

note.ja: 古英語 āgan（持つ）から。own、ought と同じ語根。「持っている（義務）」→「借りがある」。

en: A thing or being, event or process, perceptible through senses; or a fact or occurrence thereof.
A knowable thing or event (e.g. by inference, especially in science).

ex.en: The phenomenon is typical of our modern era.
ex.ja: その現象は今の時代に特有のものだ。

ex.en: Acid rain is not a natural phenomenon.
ex.ja: 酸性雨は自然現象ではない。

ex.en: It's a phenomenon I've never seen before.
ex.ja: 見たことない現象だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 phainomenon（現れるもの）から。phainein（見せる）。「現象」。複数形は phenomena。emphasis、phase と同じ。

en: Both exact and accurate.
Consistent, clustered close together, agreeing with each other (this does not mean that they cluster near the true, correct, or accurate …

From Middle French précis, from Latin praecīsus, perfect passive participle of praecīdere, from prae- (“before, in front”) + caedere (“cut; strike”), cognate with hit. Related to incise. Doublet of précis.

ex.en: What is the precise meaning of the word?
ex.ja: その語の正確な意味は何ですか。

ex.en: The precise time of their arrival isn't known.
ex.ja: 彼らが到着する正確な時間はわかっていない。

ex.en: He gave me precise instructions to do the job.
ex.ja: 彼は私にその仕事をするための明確な指示を与えた。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ cis（切る）+ e。前もって余分を切り詰めた →「正確な・精密な」。

en: A promise or vow made on entering a religious order.
The declaration of belief in the principles of a religion; hence, one's faith or religion.

ex.ja: スミス氏は職業は医師だ。

ex.en: Please introduce yourself, sir. What's your profession?
ex.ja: 自己紹介をお願いします。お仕事は何をされていますか？

ex.en: The profession is attractive to women.
ex.ja: その専門職は、女性には魅力的である。

note.ja: ラテン語 professio（公言）から。pro（前で）+ fateri（告白する）。修道誓願を公に宣言すること →「（専門的な）職業」。professor と同じ。

en: The region which the eye overlooks at one time; a view; a scene; an outlook.
A picturesque or panoramic view; a landscape; hence, a sketch of a landscape.
To search, as for gold.
To determine which minerals or metals are present in a location.

prospect.ety: From Middle English prospecte, from Latin prōspectus (“view, sight, prospect; panorama”), from prōspiciō (“to look forward”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns), from pro (“before, forward”) + speciō, spiciō (“to look, to see”). By surface analysis, pro- + -spect. Doublet of prospectus and prospekt. Etymology 1, noun sense 11 is a semantic loan from Russian проспе́кт (prospékt). The verb is from the noun.

ex.en: Our prospects for victory are excellent at the moment.
ex.ja: 今のところ、私たちが勝つ見込みは十分にある。

ex.en: There is little prospect of my success.
ex.ja: 私が成功する見込みはほとんど無い。

ex.en: What are the prospects for his recovery?
ex.ja: 彼の回復の見込みはどうなのか。

note.ja: pro（前を）+ spect（見る）。前方を見ること →「見通し・見込み・有望な人」。

en: Serving or intended to protect.
Wishing to protect; defensive of somebody or something.
Something that protects.
A condom.

protective.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin prōtēctīvus. By surface analysis, protect + -ive.

ex.en: Birds, for instance, have a special protective device.
ex.ja: 例えば、小鳥は特別な防御装置を備えている。

ex.en: Man, too, has been given protective devices against extreme temperatures.
ex.ja: 人間も極度に寒い温度に対しては、防御装置を備えている。

ex.en: Kendo is a Japanese martial art which uses bamboo swords and protective armour.
ex.ja: 剣道は竹刀と防具を使って行う日本の武道です。

note.ja: protect（守る）+ -ive。「保護する」。

en: One who, or that which, provides a service, commodity, or the means for subsistence.

ex.en: My husband isn't quite the provider he should be.
ex.ja: うちの亭主は甲斐性がない。

note.ja: provide（提供する）+ -er。ラテン語 providere（先を見て備える）。「提供者」。

A system or component that allows other components (subscribers) to receive notifications of something, such as an event.

ex.ja: 私は出版会社で働いている。

ex.en: The editor and publisher is my cousin.
ex.ja: 編集者兼出版者であるその人は私のいとこです。

note.ja: publish（出版する）+ -er。ラテン語 publicare（公にする）。「出版社」。

en: According to reports or rumors.

From reported + -ly.

ex.ja: 伝えられるところによると、その歌手は世界ツアーを計画している。

note.ja: reported（報じられた）+ -ly。「伝えられるところによると」。

en: The act of pulling back or withdrawing, as from something dangerous, or unpleasant.
The act of reversing direction and receding from a forward position.
To withdraw from a position, go back.
To withdraw military forces.

retreat.ety: From Middle English retret, from Old French retrait or retret, from Latin retractus, from retraho. Doublet of retract, retrait, and ritratto.

ex.en: He decided neither to advance nor to retreat.
ex.ja: 彼は前進も後退もすまいと決めた。

ex.en: They had no alternative but to retreat.
ex.ja: 彼らは退却するしかなかった。

ex.en: The soldiers retreated from their positions.
ex.ja: 兵士たちは自分たちの陣地から退いた。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ treat（引く）。後ろへ引く →「退却（する）・隠れ家」。

en: An inexperienced recruit, especially in the police or armed forces.
A novice.
Non-professional; amateur
To be a rookie; to go through one's inexperienced learning period in a job, team, or organization.
To haze one or more rookies as an initiation ritual.

rookie.ety: Thought to be an alteration of recruit + -ie, or from rook (“a cheat”) + -ie. Another possible origin is Dutch broekie (short for broekvent (“a boy still in short trousers”)), a common term for a shipmate. Also suggested is Irish rúca (“an inexperienced person”).

ex.en: The rookie breathed new life into the team.
ex.ja: その新人はチームに新たな生気を吹き込んだ。

note.ja: recruit（新兵）がなまった語とされる。「新人」。

en: A dish or foodstuff where at least one piece, but typically two or more pieces, of bread serves as the wrapper or container of some other…
Any combination formed by layering one type of material between two layers of some other material.
To place (an item) physically between two other, usually flat, items.
To put or set between two other events in time.
Of a meal or serving size that is smaller than a dinner.

sandwich.ety: Named after its supposed inventor, the Earl of Sandwich (see Sandwich).

ex.en: The hotel provided us with sandwiches and coffee.
ex.ja: ホテルではサンドイッチとコーヒーを出してくれた。

ex.en: Can you make do with sandwiches for lunch?
ex.ja: お昼はサンドイッチでいいですか。

ex.en: "Where is my sandwich?" "It's in the kitchen."
ex.ja: 「私のサンドイッチどこにあるの？」「台所にあるよ」

note.ja: 18世紀のサンドイッチ伯爵（Earl of Sandwich）から。トランプをしながら食べられるようにパンに肉を挟ませたとされる。

en: The act of disuniting two or more things, or the condition of being separated.
The act or condition of two or more people being separated from one another.

separation.ety: Attested in the 15th Century C.E.; from Middle English separacioun, from Old French separacion, from Latin separatio, separationem. Morphologically separate + -ion.

ex.en: The father and son met after a long separation.
ex.ja: 親子は久しぶりにあった。

ex.en: The separation of gold from sand is problematic.
ex.ja: 砂から金をより分けるのは難問だ。

ex.en: The continuous railroad grade separation projects will unite the towns divided by railroads.
ex.ja: 連続立体交差事業は線路により分断された町を1つにします。

note.ja: se（離れて）+ par（準備する・整える）+ ation。離して整えること →「分離・別居」。separate（分ける）。

With respect to sex (either of the two divisions of organisms).

en: One of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow or water.
One of a pair of long flat runners under some flying machines, used for landing.
To move on skis.
To travel over (a slope, etc.) on skis; to travel on skis at (a place), (especially as a sport).

ski.ety: From Norwegian ski, from Old Norse skíð (“stick of wood, snowshoe”), from Proto-Germanic *skīdą (“stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to cut, split”) (see also shed). Cognate with Old English sċīd (“stick of wood”) (modern shide), Old High German skit (Modern German Scheit (“log”)).

ex.en: The skies promise better weather in the morning.
ex.ja: 空を見ると朝にはいい天気になりそうだ。

ex.en: Tom can ski as well as his brother.
ex.ja: トムは兄と同じくらい上手にスキーができる。

ex.en: You will soon be able to ski well.
ex.ja: すぐ上手くスキーができるようになるよ。

note.ja: ノルウェー語 ski（木の板）から。古北欧語 skíth（割った木）。

en: An English silver penny first introduced by the Normans.
A penny issued in other countries, such as Scotland.
Of or relating to the currency of the United Kingdom, or former types of English or British coinage.
Of silver: being of standard quality.

sterling.ety: From Middle English sterling, possibly from Old English *steorling, from steorra (“star”) and -ling, in reference to the stars that appeared on certain English pennies. Alternatively, the first element may be *stēre, meaning “strong” or “stout” (compare the etymology of solidus).

ex.en: The price is given in pounds sterling.
ex.ja: 価格は英ポンドで表示されている。

note.ja: 中英語 sterling（ノルマン朝の銀貨）から。小さな星（star）の模様があったとされる。「英貨ポンド」→ 純度の高い「純銀の」→「立派な」。

en: One who performs surgery; a doctor who performs operations on people or animals.
A surgeonfish.

surgeon.ety: From Middle English surgien, borrowed from Anglo-Norman surgien, sirogen (Old French surgien et al.), from Vulgar Latin *chīrurgiānus, from Latin chīrūrgia (“surgery”), from chīrurgus (“surgeon”), borrowed from Ancient Greek χειρουργός (kheirourgós), from χείρ (kheír, “hand”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work”). Doublet of chirurgeon.

ex.en: Besides being a surgeon, he was a famous writer.
ex.ja: 彼は外科医である上に著名な作家であった。

ex.en: The surgeon operated on the patient.
ex.ja: その外科医はその患者を手術した。

ex.en: My father is an expert surgeon.
ex.ja: 父は熟練した外科医です。

note.ja: 古フランス語 serurgien から。ギリシャ語 kheirourgos（手で働く人）。surgery と同じ。

en: The act of stealing property.

theft.ety: From Middle English theft, thefte, þefte, þefþe, þiefþe, Old English þīefþ, from Proto-West Germanic *þiubīþu, from Proto-Germanic *þiubīþō (“theft”), from *þiubijaną (“to thieve, steal”), equivalent to thieve + -t (abstract nominal suffix). Cognate with West Frisian tsjeafte (“theft”), dialectal Dutch diefte (“theft”), obsolete German Diebde (“theft”), Icelandic þýfð (“theft”).

ex.en: Please tell me how the theft was done.
ex.ja: その盗難がどのようにして行われたか教えてください。

ex.en: The police brought a charge of theft against him.

en: A device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid through a space, such as a pipe, manifold, or plenum.

To control (flow) by means of a valve.

ex.ja: 元栓、しまってる。

ex.en: This valve needs to be replaced.
ex.ja: この栓は取り替えないとダメですね。

ex.ja: トムはバルブを回しました。

note.ja: ラテン語 valva（扉の片方）から。「開き戸」→「弁」。

en: A permit to enter and leave a country, normally issued by the authorities of the country to be visited.

ex.ja: ビザを入手する手続きはどうしたらいいですか。

ex.en: Could you please issue me a visa again?
ex.ja: ビザの再発給をお願いしたいのですが。

ex.en: How long is this visa good for?
ex.ja: このビザの有効期限はどれくらいですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 visa（見られたもの）から。vis（見る）。（係官が）見て確認した書類 →「査証・ビザ」。

Just before, after, or facing.
Something that lies next to something else, especially the side of a right triangle that is neither the hypotenuse nor the opposite.
Next to; beside.
Related to; suggestive of; bordering on.

The military unit under such a flag or standard.

The ability to persuade, delight or arouse admiration.
To seduce, persuade or fascinate someone or something.
To use a magical charm upon; to subdue, control, or summon by incantation or supernatural influence; to ensorcel or exert a magical effec…

ex.ja: 画家はその婦人の魅力をうまく捕らえた。

ex.ja: ローマは私にとって非常に興味のあるところです。

ex.ja: パリは日本の女性にとってとても魅力のあるところだ。

A group of people who settle an area and maintain ties to their country of origin.

en: A small, flat, baked good which is either crisp or soft but firm.
A sweet baked good (as in the previous sense) usually having chocolate chips, fruit, nuts, etc. baked into it.
To send a cookie to (a user, computer, etc.).

ex.ja: トムは、メアリーのために箱のクッキーを買った。

en: Intentionally causing or reveling in pain and suffering; merciless, heartless.
Harsh; severe.
To spoil or ruin (one's chance of success)
To violently provoke (a child) in the belief that this will make them more assertive.

cruel.ety: From Middle English cruel, borrowed from Old French cruel, from Latin crūdēlis (“hard, severe, cruel”), akin to crūdus (“raw, crude”); see crude.

ex.ja: いったい子供がそんな残酷なことをするだろうか。

ex.en: You ought not to be cruel to animals.
ex.ja: 動物に対してむごいことをしてはいけない。

ex.en: He was very hurt by her cruel words.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女の心無い言葉に感情を傷つけられた。

note.ja: ラテン語 crudelis（残酷な）から。crudus（生の・粗い）。crude と同じ語源。

The set of standards schools are required to teach all students.

ex.ja: その大学の課程は自然科学と社会科学から成り立っている。

To render an item non-mission-capable; to ground an aircraft, etc.

ex.ja: 期限前にこの仕事を仕上げなさい。

ex.ja: シカをめがけて彼は見事な１発を放った。

ex.ja: 犬たちが鹿の周りを包囲していた。

ex.en: We didn't see many deer in the forest.
ex.ja: 森の中ではあまり鹿を見かけなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 dēor（獣）から。もとは動物全般を指した。ドイツ語 Tier（動物）と同じ。

en: To swim under water.
To jump into water head-first.
A jump or plunge into water.
A headfirst jump toward the ground or into another substance.

ex.ja: 彼は水に飛び込んでから息をしようとして水面に浮かび上がってきた。

ex.en: She dived into the swimming pool.
ex.ja: 彼女はプールに飛び込んだ。

ex.ja: 塩を過剰に使うのは避けるべきだ。

ex.ja: 教育委員会が学校を管理している。

ex.ja: その島はかつてフランスに統治されていた。

To overact; to act with exaggerated emotions.

Healing; an instance of restoration of health or hit points.

en: Having the form of a line; straight or roughly straight; following a direct course.
Of or relating to lines.

linear.ety: Borrowed from Latin līneāris, from līnea (“line”) + -āris (adjectival suffix), equivalent to line + -ar. Doublet of lineal.

ex.ja: そのグラフは売り上げが直線的に増えていることを示している。

note.ja: ラテン語 linearis（線の）から。linea（線）。「直線の」。line と同じ。

en: Occurring or appearing irregularly from time to time, but not often; incidental.
Created for a specific occasion.
A person who does something only occasionally.

occasional.ety: From Middle English occasyonal, from Medieval Latin occāsiōnālis and Old French ocasionel. By surface analysis, occasion + -al.

ex.en: I have occasional pains in the stomach.
ex.ja: 時々、胃が痛むんだ。

ex.en: He doesn't travel much apart from occasional business trips.
ex.ja: 彼は時々出張することは別としてあまり旅をしない。

ex.ja: 時折雨がぱらつくでしょう。

en: Having a specific orientation (positioning or direction).
Having had an orientation (an introduction to a topic or place).

ex.ja: 彼は自己中心な人だ。

ex.ja: 僕は学問には向いていないと思うんだ。

ex.ja: その会社の強さは未来志向の戦略によって生みだされている。

en: To make a prediction: to forecast, foretell, or estimate a future event on the basis of knowledge and reasoning; to prophesy a future eve…
To imply.

predict.ety: Early 17th century, from Latin praedicō (“to mention beforehand”) (perfect passive participle praedictus), from prae- (“before”) + dīcō (“to say”). Equivalent to Germanic forespeak, foretell, and foresay.

ex.ja: すべてがトムの予言通りに進んでいる。

ex.ja: 何が起こるか予測することはできない。

ex.ja: 将来何が起こるか誰が予言できるか。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ dict（言う）。前もって言う →「予言する・予測する」。

en: The act of pursuing.
A hobby or recreational activity, done regularly.

pursuit.ety: From Middle English pursuyte, from Old French poursuite, from the verb porsuir (“to pursue”).

ex.ja: 我々はみな日々幸福を求めている。

ex.en: After a short pursuit, the police caught him.
ex.ja: ちょっと追跡して警官は彼を捕まえた。

ex.en: Most people live in pursuit of happiness.
ex.ja: たいていの人々は幸福を求めて生きている。

note.ja: pur（= pro 前へ）+ suit（追う）。ラテン語 prosequi から →「追求・追跡・趣味（追いかけるもの）」。pursue（追い求める）。

To start again after an interruption or pause.
A summary or synopsis.
A summary or account of education and employment experiences and qualifications; a curriculum vitae (often for presentation to a potentia…

resume.ety: From Anglo-Norman resumer, Middle French resumer, from Latin resumere, from re- + sumere (“to take”).

ex.ja: 彼は短い休息の後、仕事を再開した。

ex.ja: ぼくは履歴書なんか気にしないよ。

ex.en: Since the rain stopped, they resumed the game.
ex.ja: 雨がやんだので、彼らはまた試合を続けた。

note.ja: re（再び）+ sum（取る）+ e。再び取り上げる →「再開する」。名詞 résumé は「要約・履歴書」。

en: The back of any animal; especially the upper or projecting part of the back of a quadruped.
Any extended protuberance; a projecting line or strip.
To form into a ridge.
To extend in ridges.

ridge.ety:

ex.en: Is this the bus for Park Ridge?
ex.ja: このバスは、パークリッジ行きですか。

note.ja: 古英語 hrycg（背中）から。「背骨」→ 山の「尾根」→ 屋根の「棟」。

en: Not favored by fortune.

unfortunate.ety: From un- + fortunate, doublet of infortunate.

ex.ja: あいにくの時に訪ねてしまった。

variable.ety: Borrowed into Middle English in the 14th century from Old French variable, from Latin variare (“to change”), from varius (“different, various”). Equates to English vary + -able.

ex.ja: ある歌によれば、女心は変わりやすいそうだ。

ex.en: His opinions are variable.
ex.ja: 彼の意見は変化しやすい。

en: Of or relating to the reign of Queen Victoria from 1837 to 1901, or that period.

An item of furniture from that period.

Victorian.ety: From Victoria + -an (suffix forming adjectives and agent nouns), from the name of Queen Victoria (1819–1901), monarch of the United Kingdom.

ex.en: The apartment was furnished in the Victorian style.
ex.ja: そのアパートはビクトリア朝風の家具を揃えてあった。

note.ja: イギリスのヴィクトリア女王（Victoria、在位1837〜1901）の時代の。

ex.ja: 私はもう少しで優勝するところだった。

ex.ja: 彼はもう少しで成功するところだった。

ex.ja: 彼女は危うく「知らない」と言ってしまうところだった。

en: To modify.
To improve or rectify.

adjust.ety: From Middle English ajusten, borrowed from Middle French adjuster, or Old French, from Latin ad (“to, up to, towards”) + iustus (“correct, proper, exact”); Equivalent to ad- + just. ex.ja: その時計遅れているから直してくれないかい。

ex.en: They soon adjusted themselves to the new circumstances.
ex.ja: 彼らはすぐにその新しい環境に順応した。

ex.en: She soon adjusted herself to the new school.
ex.ja: 彼女じきに新しい学校に慣れた。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ just（ちょうど・正しい）。ちょうど合わせる →「調整する・適応する」。

en: Happening by turns; one following the other in succession of time or place; first one and then the other (repeatedly).

That which alternates with something else; vicissitude.
A substitute; an alternative; one designated to take the place of another, if necessary, in performing some duty.

ex.en: It was a week of alternating snow and rain.
ex.ja: 雨と雪が交互に降った一週間だった。

ex.en: There are pictures on alternate pages of the book.
ex.ja: その本は１ページおきに絵が載っている。

ex.en: There are maps on alternate pages of the book.
ex.ja: その本には１ページおきに地図がのっている。

note.ja: alter（他方の）+ nate。一方と他方を代わる代わる →「交互にする・交互の」。

ex.ja: この小説は英文学の名作の一つに数えられている。

en: The power or ability to generate an outcome.
A digital token allowing a user or process to interact in a specified way with an object that is subject to access control.

capability.ety: Formed in Modern English as capable + -ity.

ex.ja: 新しいチームには優勝する力がある。

ex.ja: 彼女はどんな障害をも克服できるすばらしい能力を持っている。

en: Relating to the part of mental functions that deals with logic, as opposed to affective which deals with emotions.
Intellectual.

cognitive.ety: From Medieval Latin cognitīvus, from Latin cognitus, perfect passive participle of cognōscō (“to get to know”) + -īvus (adjective suffix).

ex.ja: 大学では、認知科学を専攻するつもりです。

ex.en: I'm majoring in cognitive science in college.
ex.ja: 大学では、認知科学を専攻するつもりです。

en: A person or organization against whom one is competing.
A participant in a competition, especially in athletics.

competitor.ety: Borrowed from Middle French compétiteur, from Latin competitor.

ex.ja: すべての競合会社がパイの分け前を得ようとしています。

One of the players whose primary task is to prevent the opposition from scoring.

ex.ja: 防衛者達は強い抵抗を見せた。

Borrowed from Middle French dental or Late Latin dentālis, from dēns (“a tooth”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix).

ex.en: How much will it cost to get a dental cleaning?
ex.ja: 歯のクリーニングの費用はいくらですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 dens（歯）から。dent + al。→「歯の・歯科の」。dentist（歯科医）も同じ。

en: Concerning the relationships between the governments of countries.
Exhibiting diplomacy; exercising tact or courtesy; using discussion to avoid hard feelings, fights or arguments.
The science of diplomas, or the art of deciphering ancient writings and determining their age, authenticity, etc.; paleography.

diplomatic.ety: From French diplomatique and its etymon New Latin diplōmaticus. By surface analysis, diplomat + -ic.

ex.en: The two countries do not have diplomatic relations.
ex.ja: その両国は外交関係がない。

ex.en: That country broke off diplomatic relations with the United States.
ex.ja: その国は米国との外交関係を断絶した。

ex.en: Japan has diplomatic relations with China.
ex.ja: 日本は中国と外交関係がある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diploma（二つ折りの公文書）から。公文書を扱う →「外交の・外交的な（如才ない）」。

en: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber; a membranophone.
Any similar hollow, cylindrical object.
To beat a drum.
To beat with a rapid succession of strokes.

drum.ety:
Perhaps back-formation from drumslade (“drummer”), from Middle Dutch trommelslach (“drumbeat”), from trommel (“drum”) + slach (“beat”) (Dutch slag).
Or perhaps borrowed directly from a continental Germanic language; compare Middle Dutch tromme (“drum”), Middle Low German trumme (“drum”) et al. Compare also Middle High German trumme, trumbe (“drum”), Old High German trumba (“trumpet”). Compare Ancient Greek τῠ́μπᾰνον (tŭ́mpănon, “kettledrum”) whence Modern English timbre.

ex.en: Tom has been beating the drum for the project.
ex.ja: トムはそのプロジェクトをずいぶん宣伝しているよ。

ex.en: She drummed her fingers on the table.
ex.ja: 彼女は指でテーブルをとんとんたたいた。

ex.en: Jim likes to play the drum.
ex.ja: ジムはドラムを演奏するのが好きだ。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 tromme から。擬音的な語。「太鼓」→ 形が似た「ドラム缶」。

en: Of or relating to an editor, editing or an editorial.
Appropriate for high fashion magazines.
An article in a publication giving the opinion of its editors on a given topic or current event.
A similar commentary on radio or television.

ex.ja: 彼らは反植民地主義的な社説で党を全面的に支持した。

note.ja: editor（編集者）+ -ial。「編集の」→ 編集者の意見「社説」。

en: To amuse (someone); to engage the attention of agreeably.
To have someone over at one's home, or some other venue, for a party or visit.

entertain.ety:
From Middle English entertenen, from Middle French entretenir, from Old French entretenir, from entre (“among”) + tenir (“to hold”), from Latin inter + teneō (“hold, keep”). For the noun, compare French entretien.
Sense of answering a phone call in Malaysian English is influenced by Malay layan “to serve, to attend to or engage with something”.

ex.en: Intended for children, the book entertains grown-ups.
ex.ja: 子供向けに書かれているが、この本は大人も楽しませる。

ex.en: He often entertained his friends over the weekend.
ex.ja: 彼はよく友人達を週末に家に招いてもてなした。

ex.en: They gave a play to entertain their teachers.
ex.ja: 彼らは先生を楽しませるために劇をした。

note.ja: enter（= inter 間に）+ tain（保つ）。人々の間を保つ →（客をもてなして間をもたせる）→「楽しませる・もてなす」。

en: Lasting forever; unending.
Existing outside time; as opposed to sempiternal, existing within time but everlastingly.
One who lives forever; an immortal.

eternal.ety: From Middle English eternal, from Old French eternal, from Late Latin aeternālis, from Latin aeternus (“eternal”), from aevum (“age”). Displaced native Old English ēċe.

ex.en: Some people believe in eternal life after death.
ex.ja: 死後の永遠の生命を信じている人もいる。

ex.en: Keep in mind that youth is not eternal.
ex.ja: 若さは永遠ではないということを忘れてはならない。

ex.en: Let us pray for a perfect, an eternal, peace.
ex.ja: 完璧な平和を。 永遠なる平和を祈ろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 aeternus（永遠の）から。aevum（時代・永遠）。→「永遠の・不朽の」。

en: Very broad; pertaining or appropriate to large classes or groups as opposed to specific instances.
Lacking in precision, often in an evasive fashion; vague; imprecise.
A product sold under a generic name.
A wine that is a combination of several wines, or made from a combination of several grape varieties.

generic.ety: From Middle French générique, from Latin genus (“genus, kind”) + -ic.

ex.en: The doctor prescribed a generic drug to save money.
ex.ja: 医師は費用を抑えるためにジェネリック医薬品を処方した。

note.ja: ラテン語 genus（種類）から。種類全体の →「一般的な・ノーブランドの」。

en: Grandmother.
Any elderly woman, regardless of if she has grandchildren.

ex.en: My grandma injured her leg in a fall.
ex.ja: おばあちゃんが転んで、足にけがをしちゃったんです。

ex.en: If Grandma doesn't come, the children will be disappointed.
ex.ja: もしおばあちゃんが来なければ子ども達はがっかりするだろう。

ex.en: The object of the journey was to visit Grandma.
ex.ja: その旅行の目的はおばあちゃんを訪ねることでした。

note.ja: grandmother の短縮。「おばあちゃん」。

en: To take hold (of), particularly with the hand.
To figuratively take hold of or grasp.
A hold or way of holding, particularly with the hand.
Ability to resist slippage when pressed in contact with another object or surface.

grip.ety:
Verb from Middle English grippen, from Old English grippan, from a Proto-Germanic *gripjaną (compare Old High German gripfen); compare the related Old English grīpan, whence English gripe. See also grope, and the related Proto-Germanic *grīpaną.
Noun from Middle English grippe, gripe, an amalgam of Old English gripe (“grasp, hold”) (cognate with German Griff) and Old English gripa (“handful”) (cognate with Swedish grepp).

ex.en: Tom got a grip on his emotions.
ex.ja: トムは自分の感情をぐっと抑えた。

ex.en: He was in the grip of poverty.
ex.ja: 彼は貧乏にとりつかれていた。

ex.en: I have a gripping pain here.
ex.ja: ここが差し込むように痛みます。

note.ja: 古英語 gripe（つかむこと）から。grab、grasp と同系。「しっかりつかむ」。

en: The amount that a hand will grasp or contain.
A small number, usually approximately five.

handful.ety: From Middle English handful, hondful, from Old English handfull (“handful”), from Proto-Germanic *handufullō, *handufulliz (“handful”), from Proto-Germanic *handuz (“hand”) + *fullaz (“full”); equivalent to hand + full (“fullness, plenty”) or hand + -ful. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Hondful (“handful”), West Frisian hânfol (“handful”), Dutch handvol (“handful”), German Handvoll (“handful”), Danish håndfuld (“handful”), Swedish handfull (“handful”), Icelandic handfylli (“handful”).

ex.en: Only a handful of people know the fact.
ex.ja: ほんの少数の人しかその事実を知らない。

ex.en: Only a handful of people came to the meeting.
ex.ja: 会合にはほんのわずかの人しか出てこなかった。

ex.en: That boy is a handful.
ex.ja: あの子は手がかかる。

note.ja: hand（手）+ -ful（いっぱい）。「一握り」→「少数」→ 手に余る「厄介者」。

en: In a happy or cheerful manner; with happiness.
By good chance; fortunately, successfully.

happily.ety: From Middle English happily, happyly, happyliche, happylyche, equivalent to happy + -ly.

ex.en: We must keep the law to live happily.
ex.ja: 私たちは幸せに生きるために法律を守らなければならない。

ex.en: I want to happily fall in love.
ex.ja: 幸せな恋愛がしたい。

ex.en: Happily he did not die.
ex.ja: 幸運にも彼は死ななかった。

note.ja: happy（幸せな）+ -ly。「幸せに」→ 文全体を修飾して「幸いにも」。

en: Agreement or accord.
A pleasing combination of elements, or arrangement of sounds.

harmony.ety: From Middle English armonye, from Old French harmonie, armonie, from Latin harmonia, from Ancient Greek ἁρμονία (harmonía, “joint, union, agreement, concord of sounds”), either from or cognate with ἁρμόζω (harmózō, “to fit together”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to join, fit, fix together”). First attested in 1602. Doublet of harmonia.

ex.en: In sport, team harmony is vital to success.
ex.ja: スポーツではチームの和が成功には欠かせません。

ex.en: They worked in perfect harmony with each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは非常に仲良く働いた。

ex.en: The sisters lived in harmony with each other.
ex.ja: 姉妹は睦まじく暮らした。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 harmonia（つなぎ合わせ）から。→「調和・和声・ハーモニー」。

en: Not pretentious or magnificent; unpretending; unassuming.
Having a low position or a low opinion of oneself; not proud, arrogant, or assuming; modest.
People with a low position or a low opinion of themselves; those who are not proud, arrogant, or assuming.
To defeat or reduce the power, independence, or pride of.
To make humble or lowly; to make less proud or arrogant; to make meek and submissive.

humble.ety: From Middle English humble, from Old French humble, umble, humle, from Latin humilis (“low, slight, hence mean, humble”) (compare Greek χαμηλός (khamēlós, “on the ground, low, trifling”)), from humus (“the earth, ground”), humi (“on the ground”). See homage, and compare chameleon, humiliate. Displaced native Old English ēaþmōd.

ex.en: Be it ever so humble, home is home.
ex.ja: どんなに粗末でも、我が家は我が家である。

ex.en: What he ate was very simple and humble.
ex.ja: 彼の食べるものは粗末だった。

ex.en: Defeat and failure make people too humble.
ex.ja: 敗北や失敗は人間を非常に卑屈にする。

note.ja: ラテン語 humilis（低い）から。humus（大地）の仲間。地面に近い →「謙虚な・つつましい」。humiliate（低くする→恥をかかせる）。

en: Offspring resulting from cross-breeding different entities, e.g. two different species or two purebred parent strains.
Something of mixed origin or composition; often, a tool or technology that combines the benefits of formerly separate tools or technologies.
Of or composed of mixed origin or composition.
Of a car, running on both fuel (gasoline or diesel) and electricity (battery or energy from the sun).

hybrid.ety: From Latin hybrida, a variant of hibrida (“a mongrel; specifically, an offspring of a tame sow and a wild boar”). Attested since 1601, but rare before c. 1850.

ex.en: Tom encouraged Mary to buy a hybrid car.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーにハイブリッドカーを買うように勧めた。

ex.en: Tom bought a hybrid car.
ex.ja: トムはハイブリッドカーを買った。

ex.en: My car is a hybrid.
ex.ja: ハイブリッドに乗ってるよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 hybrida（雑種）から。「雑種」→「混成物・ハイブリッド」。

en: A set of keys laid out in a gridlike pattern, used for typing on a typewriter, computer, etc.
A component of many instruments, including the piano, organ, and harpsichord, consisting of usually black and white keys that cause diffe…
To type on a computer keyboard.

ex.en: I need to buy a new keyboard.
ex.ja: 新しいキーボードを買わないとな。

ex.en: The space bar is the largest key on the keyboard.
ex.ja: スペースキーが、キーボードの中で一番大きいキーです。

ex.en: Oh? You can type without looking at the keyboard. That's cool!
ex.ja: へー、キーボード見ないで文字打てるんだ。スゴイわねー。

note.ja: key（鍵・キー）+ board（板）。「鍵盤」→ パソコンの「キーボード」。

en: With respect to place; in place.
In or from the local area.

ex.ja: これらの商品の中には、地元では手に入らないものもあるかもしれない。

ex.en: The practice still prevails locally in parts of Japan.
ex.ja: その習慣は今なお日本の所々で行われている。

note.ja: local（地元の）+ -ly。「地元で」。

en: Gentle and not easily angered.
Of only moderate severity; not strict.
A relatively low-gravity beer, often with a dark colour; mild ale

mild.ety:
From Middle English milde, from Old English milde (“mild”), from Proto-Germanic *mildijaz (“mild”), from Proto-Indo-European *melh₂- (“to beat, pound, grind”).
Cognate with Scots mild, myld (“mild”), Saterland Frisian milde (“mild”), West Frisian myld (“mild”), Dutch mild (“mild”), Low German milde (“mild”), German mild (“mild”), Danish, Swedish and Norwegian Bokmål mild (“mild”), Icelandic mildur (“mild”), Latin mollis (“soft, gentle”), Lithuanian malonus (“pleasing, pleasant, kind”), Old Norse mildr.

ex.en: Spring brings mild weather after the cold winter.
ex.ja: 寒い冬の後、春は穏やかな天候をもたらす。

ex.en: Generally speaking, the climate of Japan is mild.
ex.ja: 概して日本の気候は温和である。

ex.en: Generally speaking, the weather was mild last year.
ex.ja: 一般的に言って去年は気候が穏やかだった。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「穏やかでやわらかい」。→「穏やかな・温暖な・（味が）まろやかな」。

Among elements of some collection, such that no other element is greater (with respect to some given partial order).
Something very small; a tiny part or fragment.

en: Relating to, or consisting of, or produced by molecules.
(of an element) Combined with itself and with no other element; elemental.
Any compound having a specified (range of) molecular weight(s)

ex.ja: 彼女は大学で分子生物学を研究している。

en: The time of day when the Sun seems to reach its highest point in the sky; solar noon.
The mean time of solar noon, marked as twelve o'clock on most clocks.
To relax or sleep around midday.

noon.ety: From Middle English noen, none, non, from Old English nōn (“the ninth hour”), from a Germanic borrowing of classical Latin nōna (“ninth hour”) (short for nōna hōra), feminine of nōnus (“ninth”). Cognate with Dutch noen, obsolete German Non, Norwegian non.

ex.en: I will have finished the work by noon.
ex.ja: その仕事は昼までに終わっているでしょう。

ex.en: You are supposed to be back by noon.
ex.ja: 十二時までに帰ってくるのですよ。

ex.en: I'll come at noon to pick you up.
ex.ja: 正午に車で迎えに行くよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 nona hora（第9時＝午後3時の祈り）から。祈りの時刻が早まって →「正午」。

en: At the present time; in the current era.

ex.en: Nowadays his father goes to work by car.
ex.ja: 近ごろ彼の父は車で会社に行く。

ex.en: Nowadays, a safety zone is not always safe.
ex.ja: 最近は安全地帯が必ずしも安全ではない。

ex.en: It's not easy to find a job nowadays.
ex.ja: 今はね、仕事を見つけるのも楽じゃないよ。

note.ja: now + a（on）+ days。今の時代において →「近ごろ・今日では」。

en: In an open manner; visibly.

openly.ety: From Middle English openli, from Old English openlīċe. By surface analysis, open + -ly.

ex.en: That country has openly threatened to go nuclear.
ex.ja: その国は公然と核武装するとおどしている。

ex.en: Takeda always shows his anger openly.
ex.ja: 武田君はいつも露骨に怒りを表す。

ex.en: He's openly a furry.
ex.ja: 彼ってオープンファーリーなんだ。

note.ja: open + -ly。「公然と」。

en: A brief summary, as of a book or a presentation.
To engage in an overview; to provide a brief summary.

overview.ety:

From over- + view.

ex.en: For a business owner, having a clear overview of one's entire business is vital.
ex.ja: 経営者には企業全体を俯瞰する目が欠かせない。

note.ja: over（全体を覆って）+ view（見る）。全体を見渡すこと →「概要・概観」。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to Palestine or the Palestinian people.
An Arab inhabitant of Palestine.

Palestinian.ety:

From Palestine + -ian.

ex.en: The Palestinian students sang a traditional song.
ex.ja: パレスチナの学生たちが伝統的な歌を歌った。

note.ja: Palestine + -ian。ギリシャ語 Palaistinē。聖書のペリシテ人（Philistines）の土地。

en: An administrative part of a diocese that has its own church.
The community attending that church; the members of the parish.
To place (an area, or rarely a person) into one or more parishes.
To visit residents of a parish.

parish.ety: From Middle English parisshe, from Old French paroisse (compare the obsolete variant paroch, from Anglo-Norman paroche, parosse), from Late Latin parochia, from Ancient Greek παροικία (paroikía, “a dwelling abroad”).

ex.en: The parish church is over five hundred years old.
ex.ja: その教区の教会は５００年以上前に建てられた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paroikia（近くに住むこと）から。para（そばに）+ oikos（家）。「教区」。

en: Arousing pity, sympathy, or compassion; exciting pathos.
Arousing scorn or contempt, often due to miserable inadequacy.

pathetic.ety: From Middle French pathétique, from Latin patheticus, from Ancient Greek παθητικός (pathētikós, “subject to feeling, capable of feeling, impassioned”), from παθητός (pathētós, “one who has suffered, subject to suffering”), from πάσχω (páskhō, “to suffer”). By surface analysis, path- + -etic.

ex.en: Don't say such pathetic things!
ex.ja: そんなかわいそうなこと言わないで。

ex.en: We could not bear to listen to the sick child's pathetic cries.
ex.ja: 病気の子どもの痛ましい泣き声を聞くのは我々には耐えられなかった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pathos（苦しみ・感情）から。path（感じる）+ etic。哀れを感じさせる →「哀れな・情けない」。

en: The edible starchy tuber of the plant species Solanum tuberosum.
The plant that produces this tuber.
To hit with a thrown or fired potato.
The rhythmic sound produced by a V-twin engine—a distinctive deep, throaty exhaust note.

potato.ety:
Etymology tree
Taíno batatabor.
Spanish patatabor.
English potato
Borrowed from Spanish patata, itself borrowed from Taíno batata (“sweet potato”). Doublet of batata.

ex.en: I want some potatoes. Do you have any?
ex.ja: ジャガイモをいくらかほしいのですが、ありますか。

ex.en: The sweet potato is native to South America.
ex.ja: サツマイモは、南アメリカが原産です。

ex.en: When was the potato introduced into Japan?
ex.ja: ジャガイモはいつ日本に伝えられたのですか。

note.ja: スペイン語 patata（タイノ語 batata ＝ サツマイモ）から。→「ジャガイモ」。

en: One who makes pots and other ceramic wares.
One who places flowers or other plants inside their pots.
To act in a vague or unmotivated way; to fuss about with unimportant things.
To move slowly or aimlessly. (Often potter about, potter around.)

potter.ety: From Middle English pottere, from Old English pottere (“potter”, in placenames), from Proto-West Germanic *pottārī (“pot-maker”), equivalent to pot + -er. Influenced by Anglo-Norman poter, Old French potier (“potter”). Cognate with Dutch potter (“potter”), German Low German Pötter, Pütter (“potter”). Displaced Old English synonyms lāmwyrhta (“a worker in clay, potter”, literally “loam-worker”), tiġelwyrhta (“brickmaker, potter”, literally “tile-worker”), crocwyrhta (“crocker, potter”, literally “crock-worker”).

ex.en: I already read all the Harry Potter books.
ex.ja: ハリポタは前に全部読んだよ。

ex.en: I'd like to see the sixth "Harry Potter" movie.
ex.ja: 『ハリーポッター』の6作目が観たいな。

ex.en: I want to see the sixth Harry Potter film.
ex.ja: 『ハリー・ポッター』の第6作が見たい。

note.ja: pot（つぼ）+ -er。「陶工」。

en: The selection of one thing or person over others (with the main adposition being "for" in relation to the thing or person, but possibly a…
The option to so select, and the one selected.
To give preferential treatment to; to give a preference to.

preference.ety:
From Middle French preference, from Medieval Latin preferentia. Doublet of preferans. Morphologically prefer + -ence.
Compare typologically Russian предвзя́тость (predvzjátostʹ) (<< взять (vzjatʹ), a suppletive of брать (bratʹ), which is cognate with Latin ferō).

ex.en: He should be given preference over the others.
ex.ja: 彼は他の人より優先されるべきだ。

ex.en: I don't know your preference, so please help yourself.
ex.ja: あなたの好みが分かりませんので自由にお取り下さい。

ex.en: It can be customized to suit your preferences.
ex.ja: 好みに合わせてカスタマイズできます。

note.ja: pre（前に）+ fer（運ぶ）+ ence。（他より）前に運ぶこと →「好み・優先」。prefer（より好む）。

en: A quantity of something that is part of the whole amount or number.
Harmonious relation of parts to each other or to the whole.
To divide into proper shares; to apportion.
To form symmetrically.

proportion.ety: From Middle English proporcion, from Old French proportion, from Latin prōportiō (“comparative relation, proportion, symmetry, analogy”), from pro (“for, before”) + portio (“share, part”); see portion. By surface analysis, pro- + portion.

ex.en: Robert got a small proportion of the profit.
ex.ja: ロバートは利益のほんの一部しかもらわなかった。

ex.en: This beer contains a high proportion of alcohol.
ex.ja: このビールはアルコールの含有量が多い。

ex.en: In proportion as the sales increase, the profit will rise.
ex.ja: 売り上げが増えるにつれて収益も上がる。

note.ja: pro（〜に応じて）+ portion（分け前）。分け前に応じた割合 →「割合・比率・釣り合い」。

en: Violent uncontrolled anger.
A current fashion or fad.
To act or speak in heightened anger.
To move with great violence, as a storm etc.

From Middle English rage, from Anglo-Norman rage, from Late Latin rabia, from Classical Latin rabiēs (“anger, fury”). Doublet of rabies.
Displaced native Middle English wode, from Old English wōd ("madness, fury, rage"; compare Modern dialectal English wood (“mad, insane, furious, raging”)); and Middle English hotherte (“anger”), from Old English hātheort (“fury, anger, wrath, rage”).

ex.en: He hit his brother in a rage.
ex.ja: 彼はカッとして兄をなぐった。

ex.en: He left the room in a rage.
ex.ja: 彼は激怒して部屋を出た。

ex.en: He is in a rage to know.
ex.ja: 彼は知識欲が旺盛である。

note.ja: ラテン語 rabies（狂気・狂犬病）から。→「激怒・猛威・大流行」。rabies（狂犬病）と同語源。

en: The process of bringing an object back to its original state; the process of restoring something.
The result of such a process, such as a dental restoration (a dental prosthesis).

restoration.ety: From Middle English restoracion, altered from restauracion (from Latin restaurātiō) by partly deriving from restoren + -acion. By surface analysis, restore + -ation.

ex.en: The museum is closing for restorations.
ex.ja: ミュージアムは、修復作業のため休館中です。

ex.en: The ruined castle is now under restoration.
ex.ja: 廃墟となったその城は現在修復中です。

note.ja: restore（回復させる）+ -ation。「回復・修復」→（the Restoration）英国の王政復古。

en: Holding one's own self-interest as the standard for decision making.
Having excessive or exclusive regard and concern for one's own well-being, profit or pleasure, with little or no consideration for others.

selfish.ety: From self + -ish. Compare Danish selvisk (“selfish”), Swedish självisk (“selfish”).

ex.en: Above all things, we must not be selfish.
ex.ja: とりわけ我々は利己主義になってはならない。

ex.en: Don't keep company with such a selfish man.
ex.ja: そんな利己的な男と交際してはいけない。

ex.en: His selfish attitude put my back up.
ex.ja: 彼の身勝手な態度に腹を立てた。

note.ja: self（自分）+ ish（〜っぽい）。自分のことばかり →「わがままな・利己的な」。

en: A UK army rank with NATO code OR-6, senior to corporal and junior to warrant officer ranks.
The highest rank of noncommissioned officer in some non-naval military forces and police.

sergeant.ety:
From Middle English sergeant, sergeaunt, serjent, serjaunt, serjawnt, sergant, from Old French sergeant, sergent, serjant, sergient, sergant (“sergeant, servant”), from Medieval Latin servientem, accusative of serviēns (“a servant, vassal, soldier, apparitor”), from Latin serviēns (“serving”), present participle of serviō (“serve, be a slave to”). Doublet of servant and servient.
The shift from /vj/ > /dʒ/ was a regular development in Old French. Compare cavea > cage, salvia > sage.
The fish is so called because of its stripes, supposed to resemble a sergeant's insignia of rank.

ex.en: He rose to the rank of sergeant.
ex.ja: 彼は巡査部長の地位に昇った。

ex.en: A captain is above a sergeant.
ex.ja: 大尉は軍曹よりも階級が上だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 serviens（仕える者）から。serve（仕える）と同じ。→「軍曹・巡査部長」。

en: A fine fiber excreted by the silkworm or other arthropod (such as a spider).
A thread or yarn made from silk fibers.
To develop silk.
To remove the silk from (corn).

ex.en: This beautiful dress is made of silk.
ex.ja: この美しいドレスは絹で出来ている。

ex.ja: 今絹にはわずかな需要しかない。

ex.en: I gave my father a silk tie.
ex.ja: 私は父に絹のネクタイをあげた。

en: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
An indentation, imprint, or mark made by stamping.
To step quickly and heavily, once or repeatedly.
To move (the foot or feet) quickly and heavily, once or repeatedly.

ex.ja: その珍しい切手はどこでみつけたのですか。

ex.en: John likes to trade stamps with his friends.
ex.ja: ジョンは友達と切手を交換するのが好きだ。

ex.en: This rare stamp is hard to come by.
ex.ja: このめずらしい切手は手にはいりにくいんだよ。

note.ja: 古英語 stempan（踏みつける）から。「踏む」→ 押しつける「印・スタンプ」→「切手」。stampede と同系。

en: An impressive seat used by a monarch, often on a raised dais in a throne room and reserved for formal occasions.
Leadership, particularly the position of a monarch.

throne.ety: Inherited from Middle English trone, from Old French trone, from Latin thronus, from Ancient Greek θρόνος (thrónos, “a seat, chair”). Superseded earlier seld (“seat, throne”).

ex.en: He was to succeed to the throne.
ex.ja: 彼は王位を継承することになっていた。

ex.en: He came to the throne by succession.
ex.ja: 彼は世襲によって王位についた。

ex.en: The prince succeeded to the throne.
ex.ja: 王子が王位を継承した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 thronos（高い座席）から。→「王座・王位」。

en: A strong desire to do something.
To press; to push; to drive; to impel; to force onward.
To put mental pressure on; to ply with motives, arguments, persuasion, or importunity.

ex.en: The kids urged their father to leave quickly.
ex.ja: 子供たちは早く行こうと父親をせきたてた。

ex.en: I urge you to tell him the truth.
ex.ja: 彼に対して本当のことを言うように強くお勧めします。

ex.en: My father urged me to go with him.
ex.ja: 父はついてくるように私をせきたてた。

note.ja: ラテン語 urgere（押し迫る）から。「促す・衝動」。urgent と同じ。

en: A person (now usually particularly a woman) who uses magical or supernatural powers to influence or predict events, particularly one with…
A person of any gender who harmfully employs magical power (especially innate rather than ritual)
To dowse for water.

To place or store (something, such as a document or record) in an archive (noun sense 1.1).
To transfer (less used or obsolete data, files, etc.) to a storage medium for long-term storage.

en: Clothing and ornamentation; raiment.
A collection laid out to be viewed in full.
To clothe and ornament; to adorn or attire.
To lay out in an orderly arrangement; to deploy or marshal.

array.ety: From Middle English arrayen, from Anglo-Norman arraier (compare Old French arraier, areer (“to put in order”)), from Vulgar Latin *arrēdō (“to put in order, arrange, array”), from *rēdum (“preparation, order”), from Frankish *raid or *raidā (“preparation, order”) or Gothic 𐌲𐌰𐍂𐌰𐌹𐌸𐍃 (garaiþs, “ready, prepared”), from Proto-Germanic *raidaz, *raidiz (“ready”). Compare Old English rād (“condition, stipulation”), Old High German antreitī (“order, rank”). Doublet of ready.

ex.en: The troops were in battle array.
ex.ja: 軍隊は戦闘の配置で整列していた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 areer（整列させる）から。「整列」→「ずらりと並んだもの・配列」。

stomach (an organ in animals that stores food in the process of digestion)
To position one’s belly; to move on one’s belly.
To swell and become protuberant; to bulge or billow.

en: A small stall for the display and sale of goods.
A boxlike room or enclosure just big enough to accommodate one standing person, such as a phone booth or polling booth.

ex.en: There is a telephone booth at the corner of the street.
ex.ja: あの町かどに公衆電話ボックスがある。

note.ja: 古ノルド語 búð（仮小屋）から。→「売店・ブース・（電話）ボックス」。

Crude or unfeeling in manner or speech.

ex.ja: 警官はその残虐な殺人事件の手がかりを探している。

ex.ja: 圧倒的多数がその残酷な刑罰を廃止することに票を投じた。

To determine values or solutions by a mathematical process; reckon.

en: The state of being a citizen; the status of a citizen.

citizenship.ety: From citizen + -ship. Displaced native Old English burgrǣden, equivalent to borough + -red.

ex.en: He will be given American citizenship.
ex.ja: 彼にアメリカの市民権が与えられるだろう。

ex.en: He'll be granted American citizenship.
ex.ja: 彼にアメリカの市民権が与えられるだろう。

ex.en: He acquired American citizenship.
ex.ja: 彼は米国の市民権を得た。

en: A vertical (or nearly vertical) rock face.
A point beyond which something abruptly fails or decreases in value, performance, etc.

cliff.ety: From Middle English clyf, from Old English clif, from Proto-West Germanic *klib, from Proto-Germanic *klibą.

ex.ja: もう一歩下がると、崖から落ちるよ。

ex.en: He stood on the edge of the cliff.
ex.ja: 彼はがけっぷちに立っていた。

ex.en: There is a narrow path running along the cliff.
ex.ja: 崖っぷちに沿って狭い道が通っている。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「切り立った崖」。→「崖・絶壁」。
